newsitem.title: ITALY: NKorea maize crop down 70pct after drought - UN.
newsitem.headline: NKorea maize crop down 70pct after drought - UN.

text.p: Drought in North Korea has devastated 70 percent of the maize crop and could lead to a worsening of the food situation in the famine-threatened country, U.N. agencies said in a joint statement on Monday.

"The crop is lost. It is absoulutely disastrous. It is going to be a major catastrophe that no-one realised because they kept on hoping it would rain tomorrow," Roberto Christen, an adviser with the U.N's Rome-based Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO), said in the statement.

Christen was part of a U.N.-coordinated mission to North Korea at the end of July to assess the effects of the hermit state's worst drought in 61 years on a crop already devastated by unprecendented flooding in 1995-96.
"The drought exacerbates the fragility of the agricultural production system, already weakened by two consecutive years of losses due to flood," the agencies said in the statement.
North Korea had been relying on international food aid donations to stave off famine while waiting for its October cereal harvest. The statement said rice crops could also be affected.
"Should the drought continue and less water be available for irrigation, the losses on paddyfields could also reach alarming proportions," the agencies said.
